content:
Apple TV is kicking off the fall season this week with 《Mayday》, a new film starring Ryan Reynolds that's both a buddy comedy and an action spy thriller. The first batch of reviews has been unanimously positive.

Reviews of 《Mayday》 are praising the film's action sequences, sense of humour, and chemistry between its two leads.

Apple TV is best known for its series, with current hits like 《Ted Lasso》, 《Dark Matter》 and 《Silo》 all performing well both critically and commercially. But Apple TV's film offerings are increasingly worth watching too.

In addition to 15 classic films newly added for free for subscribers, several high-profile Apple original movies are also about to be released, with 《Mayday》 leading the charge.

《Mayday》 will be available on Apple TV this Friday (4 September) (watch here).

The film stars Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh, directed by John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein — a duo previously behind 《Game Night》, 《Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves》, and co-writers of 《Horrible Bosses》.

Reviews of 《Mayday》 have just dropped, and they're almost unanimously positive. Here are some excerpts:

  • JoBlo: "《Mayday》 is definitely one of the best films this year that didn't get a theatrical release, and one of the best streaming exclusives I can think of."
  • Empire: "When you hear 'a Ryan Reynolds-starring buddy comedy action movie,' you probably already have a pretty good idea — stylish fights, endless sharp one-liners, and a thoroughly entertaining ride. 《Mayday》 delivers all of that, with a few extra surprises."
  • The Hollywood Reporter: "This popcorn movie relies on the wildly mismatched comedic chemistry of its two leads to deliver a thoroughly entertaining diversion. It leaves you wanting the sequel it hints at."

Many critics have noted that 《Mayday》 feels like — and probably should have been — a big-screen theatrical release.

Crisply executed action, appealing humour, and Reynolds' lead performance come together to make a film that, in years past, could absolutely have been a summer box-office smash.

Either way, Apple TV subscribers can stream it for free starting this week.

Apple TV costs US$14.99 per month, or can be subscribed to as part of an Apple One bundle.
